title: Learning from Positive and Unlabeled Multi-Instance Bags in Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Anomaly detection can involve multi-instance bags where labels are available for bags rather than individual instances, and in many real-world settings only positive labels are collected alongside unlabeled data.

gap.claim: No work is dedicated to learning from positive and unlabeled data in a multi-instance setting for anomaly detection.

contributions.claim: Proposes a method for learning from positive and unlabeled bags in anomaly detection using an autoencoder-based anomaly detector with a new loss.
Provides a theoretical analysis of the proposed method.
Evaluates the method on 30 datasets against multiple adapted baselines.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the method as the first method for learning from positive and unlabeled bags in anomaly detection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their method performs better than multiple baselines adapted to the proposed setting on 30 datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces multi-instance learning, in which instances are grouped into bags and labels are provided at the bag level.
Connects multi-instance learning to anomaly detection, where labels are rare and costly and positive events are often preferentially collected.
Identifies the lack of dedicated work on positive and unlabeled multi-instance anomaly detection.
Proposes an autoencoder-based method with a modified objective and new loss, and theoretically analyzes it.
Reports evaluation on 30 datasets with performance better than multiple adapted baselines.

source_observation.claim: In anomaly detection, only positive labels may be collected because they represent critical events.

interpretation.claim: Learning methods should account for asymmetric label availability instead of assuming conventional positive-negative supervision.

application.claim: For applications with critical-event labels and unlabeled observations, consider positive-and-unlabeled learning formulations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this formulation is appropriate for settings with reliable negative labels or different labeling mechanisms.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the 30 datasets or their domains.
The abstract does not specify the proposed loss, theoretical results, evaluation metrics, or baseline methods.
The abstract does not report numerical performance values or experimental conditions.
